transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-03
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Taylor Brooks (Redwood AE), Nora Patel (Redwood SE), Samir Khan (Redwood Product), Maya Singh (Atlas Head of Search), Daniel Park (Atlas Eng Manager), Priya Rao (Atlas Data Scientist)

[00:00] Taylor: Hey everyone, thanks for making time. quick intros — I m Taylor, AE at Redwood, and with me is Nora and Samir. we ll walk through hosted api embeddings and our rerank flow and live demo, and then we ll leave time for Qs.
[00:12] Maya: Hi, thanks. Excited. we re evaluating vector search and better rerank to improve our product search relevance.
[00:17] Daniel: yeah mainly latency and cost concerns, we re on a mix of managed DB and in-house microservices today.
[00:22] Nora: cool, quick product context — Redwood hosted API gives embeddings, rerank endpoints, and a full console to config routes, view per-model latency/cost, and run evals. We also have Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching/caching/quantization tuned per workload.
[00:35] Priya: can you explain rerank? we currently do candidate retrieval with elastic and then run a small NN model for scoring.
[00:40] Samir: sure. Typical Redwood flow: you call embeddings on documents (we support a few embedding families, you can use an off-the-shelf or fine-tuned embedding), store vectors in your vector DB, retrieve N candidates, then call our hosted rerank endpoint which takes the top K candidates plus the query and returns a scored ordering. The rerank model is optimized for multi-stage pipelines so it s lightweight but high-quality.
[00:58] Maya: is the rerank endpoint hosted by you or does it run close to the vectors? we worry about network hop overhead.
[01:04] Nora: good question. For our hosted product, rerank runs in Redwood s region close to request origin; if you pin to a region we can minimize cross region hops. We also provide latency SLOs for customers on dedicated capacity. For Atlas s use-case we can show p95 numbers in the demo.
[01:22] Daniel: what numbers do you typically see? we need p95 under 200ms for web storefront.
[01:27] Nora: for small K (<=10) and sequence length typical for titles/snippets, we see p95 around 90–180ms on hosted tier depending on model size and region. For our benchmark: embeddings + vector retrieval + rerank end-to-end ~ 120–240ms depending on vector DB hit. We ll share the benchmark spreadsheet.
[01:47] Priya: how are embeddings priced? cost per embedding call and per-token for rerank?
[01:52] Taylor: pricing is usage based — per-embedding vector unit and per-rerank request (combination of token and compute unit). I ll send the detailed sheet. note Optimize can reduce units via caching and batching recommendations.
[02:05] Maya: we use Pinecone today for vectors, is that similar?
[02:08] Samir: Pinecone/Weaviate are vector index providers; Redwood s hosted API returns embeddings you can store in any vector DB. Rerank is our hosted scoring layer; you can also self-host the rerank model on private/dedicated if needed. So you could keep Pinecone and add Redwood rerank on top.
[02:24] Daniel: so we could keep current index and call your rerank after retrieval?
[02:27] Nora: exactly. Many customers do that in initial POC. you get better relevance quickly without reindexing.
[02:33] Maya: curious about vector similarity — cosine vs dot product — any guidance?
[02:37] Samir: depends on vector normalization and your DB. We recommend cosine for semantic relevance typically; for some dot-product-trained embeddings dot product works better. Redwood Optimize will run evals on your logs and recommend similarity metric and scaling factors.
[02:52] Priya: can you demo a live rerank?
[02:55] Taylor: yeah Nora, you want to kick off the console demo?
[02:58] Nora: sure. I m sharing my screen — opening Redwood Console, route config, per-route metrics. Here s a search route for a commerce demo: you can see token-level cost, p95 latency, and rerank hit rate. On the right I have a sample query and top-10 candidates.
[03:18] [screenshare glitch briefly, audio drop 2s]
[03:20] Nora: okay back. I m going to run a live rerank call — using the hosted rerank endpoint — passing query + 10 candidate vectors. you ll see the returned ranking and a score for each candidate, plus explanation tokens (structured output).
[03:35] [typing sounds]
[03:40] Nora: result returned in 340ms end-to-end on this demo tenant — note dev region and small load, production p95 is typically lower with autoscaling.
[03:48] Maya: 340ms is a bit high for our SLA; but you said p95 ~120ms earlier?
[03:52] Nora: right, this demo tenant is cold and has additional logging enabled. With warm cache and optimized batching we saw 120ms in the benchmark run. Also our dedicated tier drops latency further.
[04:05] Daniel: what about caching — do you support prefix or KV cache for embeddings/rerank?
[04:09] Samir: yes we support automatic prefix/KV caching for common queries, and we have result-level caching for identical rerank requests. Optimize suggests cache TTLs based on your query frequency distribution.
[04:19] Priya: security questions — we need SSO, RBAC, audit logs, and SOC2 compliance. Do you offer VPC/private?
[04:26] Taylor: yes SOC2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC in Console, audit logs are available on Private and Dedicated with extended retention add-on. We also support Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) for regulated data and integrate with KMS/HSM for key management. I ll send the security pack link.
[04:44] Maya: good. data residency: can you keep embeddings in eu-west?
[04:48] Nora: yes, you can pin region and we can set data residency controls. For full isolation customers use Private or Dedicated.
[04:55] Daniel: one concern is cost at scale — millions of queries per day. how do you help with unit economics?
[05:01] Samir: Optimize will recommend batching, quantization of model weights for rerank on dedicated, and hybrid search (cheap lexical filtering then small K semantic rerank). We can model estimated monthly cost once we have logs.
[05:14] Priya: can rerank run on quantized models? concern about quality drop.
[05:18] Samir: yes we can run quantized rerank models; Optimize includes regression evaluation against your golden labels and only recommends quantization if quality drop is within your threshold. We ll show you a before/after eval in the POC.
[05:33] Taylor: recap — we ll send pricing + benchmarks, Nora will provision demo tenant and upload a sample rerank notebook, Atlas to share query logs and golden labels. Anything else?
[05:42] Maya: can you include a comparison matrix vs Pinecone and Weaviate for our procurement team?
[05:47] Taylor: yes I ll include a short competitor comparison sheet and feature matrix.
[05:51] Daniel: also include expected SLA numbers for hosted vs dedicated capacity.
[05:55] Nora: will include p95/p50 numbers and the autoscaling behaviors.
[05:59] [brief cross talk]
[06:05] Maya: one last technical — for the rerank input format, do you accept raw text or do we need to pass vectors?
[06:10] Samir: rerank accepts both forms. You can pass candidate ids and we ll fetch vectors if stored in Redwood-managed index, or pass in vector payloads/feature matrices if your index stays external. The HTTP shape is documented; Nora will attach a sample curl and Python snippet.
[06:26] Priya: great. would like to test different similarity metrics on our logs.
[06:29] Samir: Optimize will run tests and recommend metric and thresholds.
[06:33] Taylor: okay that s it from us — thanks everyone, we ll follow up mid-week with the assets.
[06:38] Maya: thanks, really helpful.
[06:40] Daniel: thanks all.
[06:42] [meeting end]
